Then I opened my bag and I understood the problem.
Suddenly the bus stopped and everybody got off.
In the end she walked with me and I laughed.
So what is your best memory of Paris? Tell me what happened.
At first I did not want to go to the museum alone. But that morning I took the subway anyway.
And did you find the museum?
No! I got off at the wrong station. There were no tourists, and I was a little scared.
That sounds bad. So what did you do?
Suddenly a man started to play the guitar. I sat on the floor and I forgot the museum. In the end I still remember that music, and I always laugh when I tell this.
Let me tell you what happened.
At first everything was normal.
Suddenly something happened.
I was really scared, but then I laughed.
In the end I still remember that day.

I want to tell you what happened to me on my first day in Sao Paulo. At first everything was fine. I took the bus to the school and I sat next to the window. I was very happy. Then I opened my bag and I understood the problem: I forgot my phone at home. No map, no messages, nothing. Suddenly the bus stopped and everybody got off, but I did not remember the name of my street. I was really scared for two minutes. Then an old woman looked at me and she asked, are you lost? I said yes in terrible Portuguese, and she laughed. In the end she walked with me for ten minutes and she took me to my door. It was funny and a little embarrassing, but I remember that day every time I take the bus.

This is my best memory of the trip. At first I did not want to go to the museum alone, because my French was terrible. But that morning I went. I took the subway and I got off at the wrong station. Suddenly I was in a street with no tourists, and I was a little scared. Then something wonderful happened. A man with a guitar started to play, and people stopped and listened. I sat on the floor with them for twenty minutes. I forgot the museum, I forgot my map, I forgot everything. In the end I never saw that museum, but I remember the music and the faces of those people. It was the day I understood that I could be alone in a big city and still be happy.
